annotations.title: Relationships between companies, investors and people

description: Returns the relationship graph around a company, an investment house or a person — every relationship a filed fact with the filings that prove it: who holds the company (13F, Schedule 13D/G, Form 4: share of capital), which companies hold shares of other companies (invests_in: NVIDIA in CoreWeave, Alphabet in SpaceX), its officers and directors and their roles, and who holds warrants, convertibles or preferred shares in it (holds_rights_in: AMD's warrant to Meta, Akamai's to Anthropic) — then, as sources are added, customers, suppliers, agreements, acquisitions, competitors named by the company and lenders. Private companies are nodes too (Anthropic, Nscale): named by a filing, with no price or financials. `depth: 2` adds the neighbours' relationships (who else Vanguard holds, where else a director sits). Use it when the user asks how companies are connected, who is behind a company, or what links two of them. For the full list of a company's shareholders with bounds and moves, use get_ownership; for one investor's portfolio, get_holders.

center.description: The company, house or person at the center: a ticker, a company name (listed or not: 'Anthropic'), a holder's key or name ('vanguard', 'Elon Musk'), or a typed id from a previous answer (company:nvda, holder:vanguard, person:<id>, gov:us).

depth.description: 1 (default): the center's relationships; 2: its neighbours' too.

limit.description: How many relationships at most (default 40, max 200).

minShare.description: Minimum share of capital, as a fraction (0.01 = 1%), for ownership relationships.

natures.description: Comma-separated natures within the view: owns, invests_in, holds_rights_in, insider_of, customer_of, supplier_of, agreement_with, acquired, competes_with, lends_to.

since.description: Only relationships whose proving filing is dated on or after this day (YYYY-MM-DD).

name: get_relationships
title: Relationships between companies, investors and people
